summary: Keepalive-shadowing + prefetch deadlock leading to GPU-credit squeeze in dedicated pool (prod, us-east)
description:
Issue summary:
BrightBot reported a sustained drop in batch throughput and multiple 5xx fallback events for their dedicated pool in us-east-1 beginning ~2026-03-12T10:15Z. Symptoms included prolonged GPU attach latencies, bursty 429/504s on batched routes, and fallback to lower-tier model variants.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency/p99 for embedding and chat routes spiked to 6–12s for ~30% of requests.
- BrightBot reported visible user errors and loss of throughput on reserved capacity routes for ~45 minutes.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (BrightBot-dedicated-us-east) running mixed workloads (short-stream chat + long-lived analytics keepalives).
- Platform: production, us-east-1.
- Autoscaler profile: predictive+reactive hybrid, cooldown 60s.

Timeline & observable triggers:
- 10:11Z: small increase in long-lived keepalive sessions from BrightBot analytics sidecars.
- 10:14Z: allocator heartbeats show increasing slot reservations with incomplete prefetch completes.
- 10:18Z: autoscaler issued a small scale-up, but attach latencies continued to climb and batchers started to serialize.
- 10:30Z: several in-flight prefetched KV leases exhausted, leading to short bursts of eviction and 5xx fallbacks.

Steps to reproduce (internal replication):
1) Create many long-lived keepalive streams with small periodic pings (10s) while also sending short chat bursts.
2) Configure predictive autoscaler with cooldown 60s; use dedicated-reserved pool.
3) Observe allocator slot attach times, KV prefetch success rate, and autoscaler decisions.

Observed behavior:
- Keepalive connections appear to "shadow" prefetched slots: long sessions hold soft leases preventing efficient batch coalescing.
- Prefetch pipeline enters a backpressure loop where incomplete prefetches block allocation of new batches (deadlock-like), causing GPU-credit counters to drop faster than autoscaler can replenish.
- Autoscaler scales up but new attachments take >45s and often fail to join batches, triggering immediate fallbacks.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived and long-lived streams should coexist without prefetch starvation; autoscaler should respond to increased queued demand within configured SLO.

Relevant logs & traces (snippets):
- allocator.log @2026-03-12T10:16:02Z: "soft-lease hold: session=brightbot-analytics-321 lease_ms=120000 state=prefetch_pending"
- kv-prefetcher @2026-03-12T10:17:48Z: "prefetch_timeout model=redwood-v2-7b-instruct ctx=2048 pending=87"
- autoscaler @2026-03-12T10:18:05Z: "scale_request: +2 gpus reason=queued_duration_p90>threshold"
- serving-runtime @2026-03-12T10:19:32Z: "attach_timeout session=client-1983 err=attach_latency>30000ms retries=3"

Initial hypothesis:
- A cohort of long-lived keepalives with periodic small traffic holds soft prefetch/lease state that misleads the allocator and serializes batch formation (shadowing).
- Prefetcher backpressure + autoscaler cooldowns allow GPU-credit counters to drain, causing attach stalls and cascading evictions.

References and cross-links:
- Slack: #support (thread ts: 1647839200.000200), #infra-alerts.
- Incident tracker: INCIDENT-2026-03-12-08 (internal).
- Observability: dashboards/dedicated/brightbot-us-east (p99/attach/kv-prefetch).
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate mix of long-lived keepalives and short chat bursts against a dedicated pool
Observe allocator soft-lease hold counts and kv-prefetch pending metrics
Watch autoscaler decisions and attach latencies during the spike

investigation_notes: 10:20Z SRE confirmed elevated soft-lease count tied to keepalive-heavy cohort (query: soft_lease_count{pool='brightbot-dedicated-us-east'})
10:25Z Engineering reproducer validated that when keepalives hold soft leases, new batch coalescing p99 degrades >4x
Heap snapshot of kv-prefetcher shows ~18% of prefetch worker threads waiting on socket reads (likely sidecar backpressure).
Autoscaler logs show scale recommendations applied but attach throttling prevented effective capacity increase (attach_rate limited by allocator queue)
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12T10:22Z: Reached out to BrightBot with acknowledgement and requested traffic capture (keepalive frequency + SDK version).
BrightBot (Customer) 2026-03-12T10:30Z: Sent samples and confirmed sidecar telemetry showing steady connection churn every 9–11s.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-12T10:40Z: Scoped to allocator + kv-prefetcher; spinning up repro cluster in staging to validate prefetch deadlock conditions.
Jordan Reyes (Infra Eng) 2026-03-12T11:05Z: Observed that prefetch worker queue size spikes correlate with failed attach attempts. Opening allocator instrumentation PR.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12T11:40Z: Temporary mitigation suggested to BrightBot: reduce keepalive frequency to 60s or enable connection pooling to lower soft-lease footprint.
current_workaround: Temporary mitigation in production: two options provided to customer - (1) reduce sidecar keepalive frequency to >=45–60s, (2) enable short-lived connection pooling in their SDK. Both reduce soft-lease count and restored throughput in tests. We also applied a targeted autoscaler override to speed reactive scale-ups for this customer's pool as a short-term action.
resolution: In Progress - partial customer workaround accepted; engineering reproducer created. No permanent fix yet.
follow_up_tasks: ENG: Add allocator metric to break down soft-lease holders by session type (task: ALLOC-471)
ENG: Patch kv-prefetcher to abort prefetch on long socket wait (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/prefetcher/pull/18)
SRE: Tweak autoscaler policy for dedicated pools to allow emergency fast-path overrides (runbook update)
CS: Coordinate with BrightBot to roll SDK patch that enables connection pooling and validate in staging
